objective: metric round 8, bar = HBAA +0.7012, the reference is the open lever

metrics.title: Busemann (horospherical) height of each level-1 cell under the item's full training predecessor history, converted to a full-negative-population soft expected rank
metrics.formula:
Notation. B^d is the Poincare ball of radius 1, curvature K = -1 (so c = 1); exp_x and log_x are its exponential and logarithm maps. N = 24587 items. code1(i) in {0..255} is the level-1 integer of item i in the exported SID table. s_i, t_i in B^d are the frozen Issue #126 reference's source and target representations of item i (learned on training pairs only). sigma(u) = 1/(1+e^{-u}). D_train is the training split of (history, target) pairs.
1. Predecessor history of an item (whole training history, not one pair):
   Pred(i) = the multiset union of the items j appearing in the histories of ALL training pairs whose target is i.
2. Query point: b_i = the Karcher (Frechet) barycentre of {s_j : j in Pred(i)} in B^d, computed by x_0 = 0, x_{k+1} = exp_{x_k}( (1/|Pred(i)|) * sum_j log_{x_k}(s_j) ) for k = 0..49. The query direction is the ideal boundary point xi_i = b_i / ||b_i|| in S^{d-1}. Item i is skipped if Pred(i) is empty or ||b_i|| < 10^-3; the skip set I is whatever remains.
3. Cell representatives (target side, because the decoder emits SID tokens of the target): for each level-1 code a, M_a = {j in training items : code1(j) = a}, n_a = |M_a|, m_a = Karcher barycentre of {t_j : j in M_a} in B^d (same 50-step iteration).
4. Horospherical height (the curved operation): for x in B^d and xi in S^{d-1},
   B(x; xi) = log( (1 - ||x||^2) / ||x - xi||^2 ).
   This is the Busemann function of the geodesic ray from the origin to the ideal point xi; it is constant on the horospheres orthogonal to that ray and grows without bound along it. The curvature enters through the conformal factor (1 - ||x||^2): as K -> 0 the expression degenerates into the affine projection xi . x, so the term is only score-bearing because the ball is curved.
   H_i(a) = B(m_a ; xi_i), the horospherical height of cell a as seen from item i's history direction.
5. Fixed scale (derived, never tuned): let H = { H_i(a) : i in I, a = 0..255 } be the pooled heights;
   tau = 1.4826 * median_{h in H} |h - median(H)|.
6. Soft expected rank of each item's own cell against the FULL negative population (all 256 cells, weighted by their true sizes):
   r_i = 1/2 + sum_{a=0}^{255} n_a * sigma( ( H_i(a) - H_i(code1(i)) ) / tau ),
   r_i_tilde = ( r_i - 1/2 ) / (N - 1).
7. The metric: HORO_CELL_RANK = 1 - 2 * (1/|I|) * sum_{i in I} r_i_tilde. One scalar, in [-1, +1], higher is better.
metrics.inputs: (a) the exported Stage-2 SID table: the level-1 integer code for every item (levels >= 2 are not read); (b) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference: per-item source vector s_i and target vector t_i in the shared Poincare ball, both produced from training pairs only; (c) the TRAINING split of (history, target) pairs, used solely to form Pred(i). Nothing else: no validation pair, no test pair, no recall, no Stage-3 artefact.
metrics.geometry: Curvature K = -1, Poincare ball of radius 1, c = 1 fixed by construction, not fitted. Three curved operations, all explicit: (i) Frechet/Karcher barycentres of the predecessor history and of each cell's target members, computed with exp/log maps on the ball (a mean in the interior of a negatively curved space, not a Euclidean average); (ii) the ideal-boundary direction xi_i = b_i/||b_i||, which exists because a negatively curved space has a sphere at infinity - the query is a direction, not a vector; (iii) the Busemann function B(x; xi) = log((1-||x||^2)/||x - xi||^2), a horocycle height. Where curvature bites: the factor (1 - ||x||^2) is the conformal factor of the ball, so two cells with the SAME Euclidean offset from the origin but different radii get different heights, and a cell sitting at the origin scores 0 no matter how well it points. At curvature 1e-3 the same expression collapses toward a linear projection and the metric must lose most of its correlation: that is the built-in curvature control.
metrics.why: Recall@10 is decided at level 1: the correct target must be in the winning (or near-winning) level-1 cell, because from level 2 the prefix is nearly an item identifier, so cell identity approximately equals item identity. The evidence in the collection is that the recall signal lives in the contrast between the query direction and a cell's centroid direction - that is what Q_H (+0.634) and HBAA (+0.701) exploit. This metric keeps that contrast but changes three things at once. (1) It replaces the pair-level query with the item's whole predecessor history: b_i is the barycentre of every training item that ever preceded i, so the query point averages away the noise of any single history and is a property of the item, not of one pair. (2) It replaces the alignment/distance score with a horospherical height, which is the correct way to compare points at very different radii in a ball. A centroid of small norm is weakly committed - its direction is unreliable - and a raw inner product or geodesic distance can be inflated by such a centroid merely pointing roughly the right way. The Busemann height discounts radius through the conformal factor, so a cell only scores if it is BOTH directional and radially committed, which is precisely the condition for a trie cluster to be confidently decodable. (3) It replaces the mean over ten sampled negatives with the entire negative population, through a sigma-smoothed expected rank over all 256 cells weighted by their true sizes, so a table whose true cell is high but whose whole competitor cloud sits in the same direction (the signature of a collapsed or geometry-blind partition) is penalised, and, crucially, the expected-rank form makes collapse score exactly zero with no size-matching hack: a one-code table gives every item r_i_tilde = 1/2 and HORO_CELL_RANK = 0, and a randomly relabelled table does the same because every cell centroid then sits near the global mean. That is the failure that killed the plain path likelihood (-0.49, correlated -0.78 with bucket count); here collapse is neutral by construction rather than penalised by a correction term.
metrics.compute: 50 Karcher iterations on |I| predecessor sets (total predecessor mass <= |D_train|, typically <= 2e5 items) plus 256 cell barycentres: O((|D_train| + N) * d * 50). Then |I| * 256 Busemann evaluations, each O(d): 24587 * 256 * 64 ~ 4e8 flops, fully vectorisable as one (24587, 256, d) broadcast in numpy, ~10-25 s and < 2 GB at float32. The expected-rank sum is over the 256 cell values only, not over pairs, so the rank stage is O(N * 256) sigmoid evaluations. Total well under one minute on 24587 items and 256 codes.
metrics.risks: (a) If the frozen reference over-shrinks its target vectors toward the origin, all m_a sit near 0, all heights collapse, and the metric degenerates to ~0 with no signal - the same regime that makes any radius-sensitive score uninformative. (b) Mixing sides: xi_i comes from source representations while m_a comes from target representations; this assumes the reference's two sides share one ball's geometry, which is stated in the reference's contract but is an assumption. (c) Items with empty or near-zero-norm predecessor barycentres are dropped; if that set is large for a table (rare in practice, since it depends on the split and not on the table), the remaining set may not represent the table. (d) The Karcher iteration is only approximately convergent at 50 steps; it is deterministic and identical for every table, so it cannot bias the ranking across tables, but it can attenuate small-norm centroids further. (e) If a table places all its distinguishing power at levels >= 2 while level 1 is nearly constant, this metric - like Q_H - cannot see the levels 2+ structure and will under-rate it; that is a deliberate scope choice, not a bug, because the measured evidence says level 2+ prefixes are item identifiers.
metrics.failure_mode: Worst on a RADIALLY STRATIFIED table: one that assigns level-1 codes by the norm of the target representation (shell 1 gets codes 0-15, shell 2 codes 16-31, ...) so that all 256 cells are perfectly size-balanced and each cell's target barycentre has the same direction spectrum as the whole population. Every m_a then differs from the others only in radius, the horospherical heights B(m_a; xi_i) are near-identical for all a, every r_i_tilde is 1/2, and the metric returns 0 - while the bucket count is maximal, the same-bucket ratio is unremarkable and Q_H would also be near zero, yet the table is not obviously broken by any prefix-count statistic. Second worst is the one-code table, also 0. That is the intended behaviour: this metric measures only whether the level-1 partition is directionally aligned with the training predecessor geometry, and a partition that carries no directional information scores nothing.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic free-energy cell rank — the chance-corrected soft rank of the true level-1 cell under a leave-one-out Karcher barycentre of the full training history, scored against the whole per-cell negative distribution.
metrics.formula:
Work in the open ball B^d = {x in R^d : ||x|| < 1} at constant curvature c = -1, with the Poincare Riemannian distance

  d(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2·||x-y||^2 / ( (1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2) ) ).

KarcherMean(S): the point m in B minimising sum_{y in S} d(m,y)^2, obtained by Riemannian gradient descent with step 1, initialised at the Euclidean mean of S projected by x -> x·(1-1e-6)/max(1,||x||), stopped at ||grad|| < 1e-8 or 30 iterations, whichever comes first (step 1 and the cap 30 are fixed a priori, not fitted).
beta = 1/tau_ref, where tau_ref is the contrastive temperature stored in the frozen Issue #126 reference (or its stored learned inverse-temperature scale, if that is the form it exposes).
For a TRAIN pair (q,p): let H_q = { j : (q,j) in TRAIN }, and H_q^- = H_q \ {p}; set m_q = KarcherMean({u_j : j in H_q^-}) when H_q^- is non-empty, else m_q = u_q, where u_j is the reference's SOURCE representation of item j.
For every item i != q, delta_i = d(m_q, v_i), with v_i the reference's TARGET representation of item i.
For every level-1 cell c with member set C_c = { i : code1(i) = c }, write C_c^- = C_c \ {q} (drop cells with C_c^- empty) and

  F_c = -(1/beta) · log( (1/|C_c^-|) · sum_{i in C_c^-} exp(-beta · delta_i) ).

This is the per-item free energy of the cell: a log-mean-exp soft minimum, size-neutral because the 1/|C_c^-| cancels the |C_c^-| draws. Let K_eff be the number of cells with C_c^- non-empty, let c_p = code1(p), and let sigma(z) = 1/(1+exp(-z)). Then

  pi_q = 1 + sum_{c != c_p} sigma( beta · (F_{c_p} - F_c) )
  r_q  = 1 / pi_q
  M    = (1/|TRAIN|) · sum_{(q,p) in TRAIN} r_q  -  2/(K_eff + 1).

Higher means better. The subtracted constant is the exact chance level, not an estimate: it is precisely 1/pi_q in the all-cells-tied configuration, so an uninformative table scores 0 and a one-code table (K_eff = 1) scores exactly 0.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported SID table, level-1 integer code per item only (levels 2..L are read but never used); (2) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference — per-item source representation u_i, per-item target representation v_i, and its stored contrastive temperature tau_ref; (3) the TRAINING split, used only as the pair list and for building H_q. Nothing else: no validation pair, no test pair, no recall, no Stage-3 artefact, no fitted quantity.
metrics.geometry: curvature enters in three places. In d, which is the Poincare-ball Riemannian distance at c = -1 and not a Euclidean distance in disguise: it diverges as either argument nears the boundary, so a cell whose members sit close to the sphere is penalised far more than its Euclidean offset suggests. In m_q, the Riemannian (Karcher) barycentre of the history's source points — the arithmetic mean of the same points is a different point of the ball, so the query location is itself curvature-dependent. And in F_c, which is a log-partition function of the per-item distance distribution, i.e. a soft minimum over the whole negative population. Curvature is fixed at exactly c = -1, nothing is tuned; beta = 1/tau_ref is inherited from the frozen reference rather than fitted.
metrics.why: Stage 3 walks the code tree and can only re-rank the ten items its beam reaches, so Recall@10 is capped by whether the true item's level-1 cell is reachable for the query. This metric measures that reachability directly, with the frozen reference as arbiter: for each training query it asks where the cell containing the reference-nearest item to the query's whole training history sits in a soft ordering. It adds three things over HBAA and Q_H. First, it keeps HBAA's full-history barycentre but replaces the mean over ten negative barycentres with the free energy of the entire per-cell negative population, so a cell hiding one negative almost exactly on the query is penalised instead of having it averaged away — and the Stage-3 re-rank is exactly a competition against the single best negative, not against an average. Second, it is an order statistic over the item distribution and therefore sensitive to the left tail of the negatives, the one information source the brief identifies as still unused; a mean cannot see that tail. Third, its collapse behaviour is analytic rather than empirical: the K_eff chance offset plus the 1/|C_c^-| normalisation forces one-code, few-code and relabelled tables to 0, which is precisely what sank plain path likelihood (-0.488) and its collapse reward, and it does so without any size-matched shuffling null (whose bad construction already showed up as +0.061 in hbaa_size_matched_kept).
metrics.compute: one Karcher mean per training pair over |H_q|-1 history points (|H|·30·d flops, negligible), plus one distance vector over N = 24587 items (24587·d flops) and one segmented log-mean-exp over 256 cells. The distance vectors dominate and are formed as a chunked GEMM (chunk x d) @ (d x 24587) against precomputed ||v_i||^2, followed by arcosh: 1e4 pairs at d = 64 is about 1.6e10 flops, roughly 10-20 s on BLAS; 5e4 pairs is about 50-60 s. Memory is one 24587-vector per query plus the 24587 x 64 representation matrix (~6 MB), all dense float arrays. Because only level 1 is used, K_eff <= 256 and the cell reduction is O(N) per query, so the whole thing finishes inside a minute on 24587 items.
metrics.risks: (i) if the reference's candidate set is narrower than the full catalogue, the free energy is taken over a different population than Stage 3 ranks, which flattens the signal; (ii) if the reference exposes only a learned inverse temperature and not a temperature, beta falls back to beta = 1 in curvature-normalised units — this changes the sharpness of the soft minimum but not the ranking argument, and the chance offset is unaffected because it contains no beta; (iii) the segmentation assumes code1 is the exported level-1 column and that padding/duplicate sentinel codes are excluded, otherwise empty sentinel cells enter K_eff and inflate the subtraction; (iv) a singleton history falls back to m_q = u_q, reintroducing a direct source-target comparison for that one pair (bounded, but noisier); (v) with very skewed reference norms, d saturates, many cells tie in F_c and M is driven to the chance level 0 rather than to a false positive; (vi) it shares HBAA's dependence on the reference's source/target alignment, so a weak reference weakens it too.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on a HUB-AND-SPOKE level-1 table, where each of the K cells holds one geodesically central medoid item plus uniformly random remaining items. The medoid pins every cell's free energy to nearly the same value, so F_{c_p} - F_c is near 0 on every pair, the sigmoids sit at 1/2, pi_q tends to (K_eff+1)/2 and M tends to 0 (slightly negative where the true cell's medoid happens to be the furthest). Second worst on extreme size skew — one very large cell plus 255 singletons — because the large cell wins the soft minimum for every query, true singleton cells accumulate exceedance, and M goes below 0. In both cases the table has thrown away the information that would let a prefix-restricted beam reach the right items, and the metric correctly reports no value instead of rewarding the collapse.

metrics.title: Curvature-corrected hyperbolic history-to-cell pointwise mutual information of level-1 SIDs
metrics.formula: Work at curvature c = 1 (if the frozen reference stores c_ref, replace 1 by c_ref everywhere below; the formula is stated at c = 1 WLOG). For a nonzero vector v in R^d set E(v) = tanh(||v||/2) v/||v|| and E(0) = 0 (the exponential map at the origin of the unit Poincare ball); for x in the open unit ball set L(x) = 2 artanh(||x||) x/||x|| and L(0) = 0 (the inverse, log map). For a finite set X of ball points set B(X) = E( (1/|X|) * sum_{x in X} L(x) ) (the one-step tangent/Karcher barycentre; a curved barycentre). For p,q in the ball set p (+) q = ((1 + 2<p,q> + ||q||^2) p + (1 - ||p||^2) q) / (1 + 2<p,q> + ||p||^2 ||q||^2) and d(p,q) = 2 artanh(||(-p) (+) q||). Let T be the set of training items, N = |T|, and let s = sqrt( (1/(2N)) * sum_{i in T} ( ||eS_i||^2 + ||eT_i||^2 ) ), where eS_i and eT_i are the frozen reference source and target vectors of item i. Put xS_i = E(eS_i / s) and xT_i = E(eT_i / s). Let code1(i) in {1,...,K} be the integer level-1 code of item i and n_k = #{i in T : code1(i) = k}. For every k with n_k > 0 set C_k = B({xT_i : i in T, code1(i) = k}). Let U be the set of training (query, positive-target) pairs u = (H_u, i_u^+) with nonempty query history H_u; set q_u = B({xS_j : j in H_u}) and k_u^+ = code1(i_u^+). Let tau = 1/beta_ref, where beta_ref is the frozen inverse temperature (logit scale) stored with the reference; if the reference stores a temperature T_ref instead, tau = T_ref. Then p_u(k) = exp(-d(q_u,C_k)/tau) / sum_{j : n_j>0} exp(-d(q_u,C_j)/tau), and the metric is M = (1/|U|) * sum_{u in U} [ ln p_u(k_u^+) - ln(n_{k_u^+} / N) ]. Higher M is better. Queries with empty history are skipped; codes with n_k = 0 are omitted from the softmax denominator.
metrics.inputs: (i) the exported SID table: one integer level-1 code code1(i) per training item; (ii) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference: per-item source and target vectors eS_i, eT_i for training items and its frozen beta_ref (or T_ref), learned on training pairs only; (iii) the TRAINING split: the training item set T and the training (query-history, positive-target) pairs U. Nothing else: no validation item, no test item, no validation/test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
metrics.geometry: The unit Poincare ball with constant negative curvature -1. E and L are the exp/log maps at the origin, d is the geodesic distance, (-p)(+)q is Moebius addition, and B is a geodesic barycentre computed as exp_0 of the tangent-space mean of log_0. Curvature enters in three places: the map E(e/s) that puts the Euclidean reference vectors on the ball, the log/exp pair used to form every cell and history barycentre, and the geodesic distance d inside the softmax. At c -> 0 all three reduce to Euclidean means and Euclidean distances, so the construction is explicitly a curved one, not a Euclidean distance renamed.
metrics.why: Stage 3 retrieves the target's level-1 cell from a source query, so a table is good when the target's cell is the one the query's whole history points to, against the whole field of competing cells. HBAA scores only a mean positive-minus-negative margin with a single tangent direction; it is blind to how the positive cell competes against the full set of cells and can be carried by one far negative. M instead uses (a) the full training history as the query point (a hyperbolic barycentre of its source items, more stable than a single anchor), (b) the full negative distribution through a log score over all K cells, which is a proper scoring rule: it rewards putting softmax mass on the true cell and penalises near-ties, and (c) the size-matched null ln(n_k/N), which removes the free mass that large or collapsed cells obtain and makes a random relabelling score 0. A table with fewer, purer cells wins only if the softmax mass on the positive cell exceeds what its size alone predicts; a table that shreds the reference neighbourhoods into cells that lose the softmax is penalised. This is more information than Q_H (a single prefix rank) and more than HBAA (a single mean margin), and it is not a count, collision or same-bucket statistic.
metrics.compute: One pass over T to compute s, the per-item maps xS_i, xT_i, the counts n_k, and the K barycentres C_k (K <= 256); one pass over U' to compute q_u; then a single |U'| x K geodesic-distance matrix and a softmax per row. Cost is O((N+|U'|) d + |U'| K d), with N = 24587 and K <= 256. All operations are closed-form and vectorisable in NumPy; no iteration beyond one tangent-mean step, no training, no pairwise item-item matrix. On 24587 items and 256 codes this is well under a minute per table, and the same xS_i, xT_i and C_k can be cached across the 97 tables because only code1 changes.
metrics.risks: (1) If the reference's source and target towers do not live in a comparable space, the cross distance d(q_u,C_k) is meaningless; the construction assumes the usual shared contrastive retrieval space. (2) If beta_ref is very large the softmax is one-hot and M is dominated by a few confident queries; if very small it is near-uniform and all tables score near 0. beta_ref is frozen, never fitted on the 97 recalls. (3) Very rare cells (n_k = 1) receive a large log(N) gain when hit, so a table that isolates a few highly predictable items can be rewarded; at K <= 256 and N = 24587 this affects a bounded minority of cells. (4) The history barycentre is undefined for cold-start queries with empty history; those queries are skipped, so a table could in principle look good on the warm subset only. (5) If the SID level-1 partition is already almost perfectly aligned, M saturates as p -> 1 and differences between near-perfect tables shrink (ceiling effect).
metrics.failure_mode: M is worst on an anti-aligned table: a table with the same K and the same cell-size multiset n_k as a good table, but whose level-1 assignment is a permutation that sends each item to a cell whose target barycentre is far from that item's reference neighbourhood (for example, codes assigned by a hash of the antipodal target direction). Then p_u(k_u^+) is near 0 while n_{k_u^+}/N is still of order 1/K, so every term is strongly negative and M is strongly negative. It is exactly 0 on the one-code table (p = 1, n/N = 1) and approximately 0 on any size-matched random relabelling (p_u(k) ~ n_k/N), so collapse and count-balance cannot be rewarded.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic behaviour-midpoint common-ancestor expected-rank alignment of level-1 SID cells
metrics.formula: Work in the unit Poincare ball B^d={x in R^d:||x||<1}, curvature -1, with Mobius addition (+), d_H(x,y)=2*artanh(||(-x)(+)y||), log_x(y)=2*artanh(||(-x)(+)y||)*((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||, exp_x(v)=x(+)(tanh(||v||/2)*v/||v||). If the frozen reference uses curvature -k, first map every point x -> sqrt(k)*x and divide every distance by sqrt(k); M is invariant because Gamma and tau scale together, while the curvature still sets the geodesics and barycentres, so the construction stays non-Euclidean. For each training item j let s_j, t_j be its source and target ball points. Define the behaviour midpoint m_j = exp_{s_j}(0.5*log_{s_j}(t_j)). Let F(S) be the Frechet barycentre argmin_{x in B^d} sum_{p in S} d_H(x,p)^2, computed deterministically by 200 Riemannian gradient steps x_{k+1}=exp_{x_k}(-(1/(1+k))*grad f(x_k)) from the Lorentzian centroid (lift to the hyperboloid, sum, renormalise), to 1e-8. For a level-1 code c let a_c = F({m_j : j in TRAIN, c_1(j)=c}). For training pair r (history H_r, positive p_r, negative set N_r) let u_r = F({s_j : j in H_r}). Define the metric Gromov product Gamma_r(c) = 0.5*( d_H(u_r,0) + d_H(a_c,0) - d_H(u_r,a_c) ) (distance from the origin to the common ancestor of the query and the cell in a CAT(-1) space). Let sigma(z)=1/(1+exp(-z)). With tau = tau_ref * Rbar, where tau_ref is the frozen reference temperature and Rbar = (1/C)*sum_c d_H(0,a_c) over the C anchored level-1 cells, define rho_r = (1/|N_r|) * sum_{n in N_r} sigma( (Gamma_r(c_1(n)) - Gamma_r(c_1(p_r))) / tau ), and M = 1 - (2/R) * sum_{r=1}^{R} rho_r. M in [-1,1], higher is better; all-equal alignments give rho=0.5 and M=0 exactly.
metrics.inputs: the exported Stage-2 SID table (integer level-1 code c_1(i) per item, 24587 rows, <=256 codes); the frozen Issue #126 reference's TRAIN-split source s_j, target t_j per item, TRAIN training pairs (H_r, p_r, N_r, |N_r|=10), curvature and temperature tau_ref; the TRAIN split. Nothing else: no validation or test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
metrics.geometry: explicit negative curvature -1. The curvature enters three times: (i) m_j is the geodesic midpoint of [s_j,t_j] (a Euclidean midpoint is a different point whenever the segment is off-origin); (ii) a_c and u_r are Frechet barycentres minimising a sum of squared hyperbolic distances; (iii) Gamma is the metric Gromov product, i.e. the depth of the common ancestor, computed with d_H, the hyperbolic analogue of a tree-prefix depth. The logistic is applied in these Gromov units, so the number is not a Euclidean distance in disguise: it is a monotone function of a hyperbolic common-ancestor depth, with geodesic-midpoint anchors.
metrics.why: a Stage-3 run retrieves by matching the query to a prefix cell; recall@10 is high when the cell holding the true next item shares a deep semantic ancestor with the user history and when the cell points toward where the item's behaviour should go. HBAA measures the first half on source-only anchors with a mean margin over ten negatives. This metric (a) puts the item side on the geodesic midpoint between source and target, so a table whose cells are coherent in the reference's behaviour-update direction scores above one that merely clusters static sources; (b) replaces the mean of ten negative margins with the full temperatured expected rank, so a table is penalised when even a few negatives sit at or above the positive cell, which is what costs top-10 recall; (c) is zero for any table that does not order cells, so collapse cannot buy score. Over Q_H it adds the frozen reference's continuous curved geometry and its target side at all, rather than a learned prefix ranking score.
metrics.compute: O(N*d) midpoints plus O(200*N*d) for the C<=256 Frechet barycentres (batched), plus O(sum_r |H_r|*d) for the queries and O(R*10) sigmoids. On 24587 items and 256 codes this is a few vectorised numpy passes over 24587 x d and 256 x d arrays; well under one minute, no training.
metrics.risks: the target representation may be noisier or in a slightly different space than the source, so m_j could be worse than s_j (it degrades gracefully to the source anchor as t_j -> s_j); tau_ref may be stored as a unit-normalised logit temperature, in which case the Rbar rescaling is what makes it dimensionally meaningful, and a mis-scaled tau only saturates or flattens rho without changing the sign; cells containing no TRAIN item have no anchor and are dropped from N_r (positives always have one); a very small R or |N_r| makes M noisy; the Frechet solver must be seeded identically across tables or it adds jitter.
metrics.failure_mode: the all-one-code table, where every item has the same level-1 code, is worst: all Gamma_r(c) are identical, every sigmoid is exactly 0.5, rho_r = 0.5 and M = 0. A uniformly random relabelling of the 256 codes onto the same item set also gives M ~ 0 because the anchors carry no history alignment. Any table that is a refinement with cells whose midpoint anchors are exchangeable with respect to the history is scored at the random baseline, never above it.
